method.trials: One worker per variant, one real-page revision each. Both received the same late reminder to preserve failed checks and distinguish edited-figure measurements from whole-page claims. No rubric or other output was supplied.
method.candidate_continuation: The initial candidate completed before receiving the final restored wording. The same worker reread the final skill, checked the existing artifact and evidence bindings, and found no changes needed. Initial artifacts were preserved. This is a continuation, not a fresh trial of the final text.
method.grading: A separate agent reads frozen criteria, source evidence, actual HTML, scripts, saved checks, and rendered previews under hidden X/Y identities. It does not receive skill texts or contract reviews.
method.private_evidence: Raw team input, generated pages, source witness, status capture, patches, scripts and screenshots remain in local scratch. Public evidence contains hashes and aggregate findings, so it cannot reproduce execution alone.
method.publication: Same-path local file publication with version labels; no external deployment or live publication race tested.

contract_review.scope: Read both complete skill files and all 16 corpus scenarios. Compared normative requirements, defaults, exceptions, provenance, evidence limits, and diagnostic examples. Did not apply either skill operationally.
contract_review.summary: All 16 scenarios retain their principal operational behavior. One citation requirement is less specific, authorship granularity is less explicit, and the description of prior validation changes. Some scenario rationales lose explicit wording. The removed checklist and red-flag lists largely duplicate retained requirements.

findings.subject: Line-number baseline must be a commit, not any revision
findings.baseline: The containing paragraph or table says which commit the line numbers belong to.
findings.candidate: State the line-number revision in the containing paragraph or table.
findings.impact: Revision can mean a branch or tag. The full-hash rule still governs durable links, but no longer explicitly requires the accompanying paragraph/table to identify the commit for the line numbers. A citation using a moving revision in prose could satisfy the new local wording.
findings.recommendation: Replace line-number revision with commit the line numbers belong to.
findings.corpus_coverage: Not directly exercised: branch-link scenario covers link targets, not the required textual baseline for path:line citations.

findings.subject: Contribution-level authorship
findings.impact: A list of names can satisfy authorship without stating who wrote which parts. Candidate retains attribution-preservation checks, but these do not restore contribution detail.
findings.corpus_coverage: The prose-pass scenario checks retention of an attribution line, not contribution-level completeness.

findings.subject: What has and has not been tried
findings.baseline: Conventions held across the originating team pages; they were not tried on another audience, and reading-time/word-count defaults are that team's.
findings.candidate: Other audiences, reading-time estimates, and word-count defaults remain untested.
findings.impact: The candidate turns limited validation outside the originating team into an unqualified statement that its time and word-count defaults are untested. This is more pessimistic, but not the same evidence claim.
findings.recommendation: Say other audiences remain untested and reading-time/word-count defaults are the originating team's.
findings.corpus_coverage: Beta scenario retains override behavior but does not distinguish this provenance change.

nonblocking_observations.subject: Status revisions
nonblocking_observations.detail: Baseline says append a dated footer paragraph; candidate says update a dated footer paragraph as one of four touches. The footer still requires one paragraph per revision, so history preservation survives when reading the whole file. Restoring append would eliminate local ambiguity.

nonblocking_observations.subject: Explicit diagnostic explanations
nonblocking_observations.detail: The no-revision/cannot-re-derive explanation, the first-change-drift explanation, and reader-decides-from-summary explanation were removed. Their operative requirements remain; a model may no longer reproduce the exact rationale expected by scenarios 6, 11, and 14.

nonblocking_observations.subject: Removed examples and evidence
nonblocking_observations.detail: Seven measured overflows missed by estimates becomes a generic missed-overflow statement; the important distinction remains. The example that technical-prose caught factual errors was removed, but the mandatory prose pass remains.

nonblocking_observations.subject: Checklist and red flags
nonblocking_observations.detail: Most are restatements of surviving rules. The warning against a footer paragraph with no board change is no longer explicit; interpreted as status-history consistency it follows from the retained four-touch rule. Read literally as applying to all revisions, the old warning conflicts with revision paragraphs for non-status edits, so its removal is not treated as a clear contract regression.

nonblocking_observations.subject: Corpus is not a complete oracle
nonblocking_observations.detail: Two-line chat behavior is inferred from scope in both versions. The table scenario says three or four at most, whereas both versions state a target, not a hard upper bound.

independent_behavior_grades.method: Independent blinded artifact assessment against the ten frozen criteria. Only the assigned trial directories and permitted shared inputs were read; no skill text, mapping, contract review or source repository was read. Actual HTML, revision/publication/check scripts, saved browser results and selected rendered rasters were inspected. Independent read-only checks compared snapshot states and revisions, immutable citations, publication equality, render-source binding, preserved figures/listings/IDs/attribution/footer note, unchanged body regions, directed graph endpoints and saved label geometry. No worker output was modified and no publication script was invoked.

evidence_types.independently_observed: File contents and comparisons, source/result bindings, script logic, preserved structure, selected saved screenshots and independent calculations over saved browser geometry.
evidence_types.worker_execution_evidence: Saved Chromium metrics/font/theme results and static assertion results; verified against final page bytes but not independently rerun.
evidence_types.worker_report_only: Cold-read process, exact initial read chronology, earlier execution escalation and absence of outside actions beyond inspected scripts.

criteria.name: Progress consistency
criteria.evidence: All 17 rows agree with the supplied snapshot: six merged, three ready, two approved, five unstarted, and one awaiting re-review. The header agrees. The historical prerequisite links remain distinct from the unstarted migration, and earlier-head approval is qualified.
criteria.limits: The snapshot is a trial premise; this review did not query the external service.

criteria.name: Author report versus confirmation
criteria.evidence: The affected migration row and header attribute completed fixes to the author and leave independent re-review pending. They do not promote that report to reviewer approval.
criteria.limits: The author report is the supplied scenario premise; the reviewer did not independently validate the fixes.

criteria.name: Coordinated revision metadata
criteria.evidence: The affected PR cells carry the expected checked revisions or merge dates; row state classes agree with their state cells. Board date, main revision and dated footer update agree. The original attribution paragraph remains byte-identical.
criteria.limits: Short display revisions are checked against the full supplied snapshot; no current repository inspection was performed.

criteria.name: Immutable source citation
criteria.evidence: The actual citation URL exactly matches the supplied repository, full immutable revision, source path and line. Its visible source reference is accurate, and adjacent prose limits the witness to source presence rather than a successful build or behavior test.
criteria.limits: The file witness was supplied; no application build or behavioral validation was run by this reviewer.

criteria.name: Edited figure semantics and accessibility
criteria.evidence: The requested human-facing heading and implementation identifier remain visible. Caption and accessible description agree. An independent comparison of actual SVG endpoints confirms all six directed connections retain their source and destination boxes. The original figure anchor and numbering remain.
criteria.limits: This confirms preservation of the supplied diagram, not independent correctness of the underlying system design. One inherited duplicate SVG marker identifier remains, and the handoff explicitly records it. Its presence did not alter the observed requested figure relationships.

criteria.name: Browser label measurements
criteria.evidence: Saved Chromium measurements are bound to the final page bytes and include all 40 edited-figure labels. Saved results show the declared fonts loaded and no final containment, free-label/shape, text/text, connector/text or viewBox failures. The reviewer inspected the measurement scripts, independently checked saved label boxes for unrelated rectangle intersections, and visually inspected desktop and narrow-screen figure rasters. The final desktop dark and narrow light rasters were viewed directly.
criteria.limits: Browser execution was performed by the trial worker; this reviewer inspected its scripts, results and screenshots rather than launching another browser. Geometry coverage is the edited figure only.

criteria.name: Theme tokens and narrow-screen behavior
criteria.evidence: Actual edited SVG colors use page tokens or currentColor. Saved browser results cover 12 combinations of desktop/narrow width, system light/dark and automatic/explicit theme; backgrounds and document widths match expectations. The scrolling wrapper and SVG minimum width remain in actual CSS, and narrow screenshots show locally clipped scrolling content with the surrounding page contained.
criteria.limits: Saved automated theme assertions primarily cover page background and overflow, rather than every computed SVG color. SVG token usage and the available light/dark rasters supply additional evidence.

criteria.name: Publication reconciliation and versioning
criteria.evidence: The revision starts from a saved current-publication baseline; the publication-only footer note survives byte-for-byte. The publication script rereads the destination and rejects unexpected intervening bytes. The final editing and publication files are byte-identical, and the local log records a version and actions.
criteria.limits: The baseline, scripts, log and resulting files support reconciliation; the reviewer did not replay a write or independently observe the initial baseline read.

independent_behavior_grades.comparison: Both final artifacts satisfy all ten frozen criteria. The evidence does not establish a behavioral regression between labels. One label retains and discloses an inherited duplicate marker, while the other repairs it; this is outside a demonstrated failure of the requested preserved figure behavior.
